blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Time, in a supply chain, is not merely a measurement — it is a competitive weapon. A company that can respond to a customer order in three days has options that a rival taking three weeks simply cannot afford. It can hold less inventory. It can follow demand more closely. It can promise better service. And, crucially, it can react to a competitor's move while that competitor is still committed to a slower cycle.

Speed, however, is built, not bought. It comes from short, reliable processes, from tight feedback loops between planning and execution, from technology that removes manual hand-offs, and from a culture that treats delay as a problem to fix rather than a fact to accept. None of these is dramatic on its own. Together, over years, they open a gap that a slower competitor finds very hard to close.

Rarely do the firms that compete on time win by being technically smarter. They win by being quietly, consistently faster — across a thousand small steps that nobody else bothered to notice.

items.q: According to the text, what advantage does a three-day responder hold over a three-week rival?
options: It always operates at a lower cost base
It can hold less inventory and follow demand more closely
It can outsource its planning function
items.why: "It can hold less inventory. It can follow demand more closely." — são justamente as opções que a velocidade abre.

items.q: What does "Speed, however, is built, not bought" imply?
options: Speed is the result of accumulated internal change, not a single purchase
Speed is too expensive for most companies
Speed can be acquired by purchasing new software
Speed matters less than cost control
items.why: Inferência: "built, not bought" contrasta construção interna (processos, cultura, loops) com uma compra pontual.

items.q: The author suggests that each individual driver of speed is…
options: undramatic alone, but powerful in combination over time
irrelevant unless the company is large
items.why: "None of these is dramatic on its own. Together, over years, they open a gap…"

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Faster firms can react while rivals are locked into a slower cycle.
Culture influences how an organisation treats delay.
A slower competitor struggles to close a time gap once it opens.
Firms that compete on time usually win by being technically smarter than everyone else.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz explicitamente "Rarely do the firms that compete on time win by being technically smarter" — a vitória vem da consistência, não da esperteza técnica.

items.q: The phrase "a thousand small steps that nobody else bothered to notice" suggests that the advantage is…
options: built on one bold, visible innovation
hard to imitate because it is diffuse and cumulative
impossible to sustain beyond a single year
items.why: Inferência: se o ganho está espalhado em mil passos discretos, é difícil de copiar — não há uma alavanca única a replicar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry apresentando sua análise à diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, I've spent three weeks trying to work out why they keep winning against us, and honestly, I expected to find a cost story. I didn't. Their landed cost sits within a percent of ours — near enough identical.

Not until I laid the two order cycles side by side did the picture come into focus. From the moment a customer confirms to the moment we ship, we run at about nine days. They run at seven. Two days. That's the whole thing.

Now, two days sounds trivial, but think about what it buys them. They can quote a shorter lead time, so they win the tighter deals we can't touch. They carry less safety stock, so their working capital is leaner. And when a price moves, they've already delivered while we're still committed to yesterday's cycle.

Rarely does an advantage like this come from one clever fix. Theirs is built from small things — a planning hand-off they automated, a feedback loop between the desk and the warehouse we simply don't have. None of it is dramatic. Added up, over three years, it's why they're pulling away. My recommendation is that we stop chasing cost and start attacking cycle time.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Harry expect to find when he began his analysis?
options: A cost disadvantage explaining the losses
items.why: "I expected to find a cost story. I didn't." — ele esperava um problema de custo.

items.q: What is the difference in order-cycle time between the two companies?
options: About two days — nine versus seven
items.why: "We run at about nine days. They run at seven. Two days."

items.q: According to Harry, what does the two-day advantage let the competitor do?
options: Quote shorter lead times and carry less safety stock
Avoid holding any inventory at all
Operate with a much larger workforce
items.why: "They can quote a shorter lead time… They carry less safety stock, so their working capital is leaner."

items.q: When Harry says "they've already delivered while we're still committed to yesterday's cycle", he implies that the rival…
options: can act on new market conditions before Harry's firm can respond
holds far more stock as a buffer
delivers late but at lower cost
items.why: Inferência: sendo mais rápido, o concorrente já reagiu ao movimento de preço enquanto a empresa de Harry ainda está presa ao ciclo anterior.

items.q: What does Harry ultimately recommend?
options: Cutting costs more aggressively than the competitor
Shifting focus from cost to attacking cycle time
Hiring more sales staff to win tighter deals
items.why: "We stop chasing cost and start attacking cycle time."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "For this business, speed is not a nicety — it is a competitive weapon." A competitive weapon is…
options: a capability used to gain advantage over competitors
items.why: Competitive weapon = arma competitiva: algo que você usa para ganhar vantagem sobre a concorrência.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "With a faster cycle, we can ___ and free up the working capital tied to it."
items.why: Hold less inventory = manter menos estoque, o que libera capital de giro.

items.q: "A tight feedback loop between the desk and the warehouse catches errors within hours." A feedback loop is…
options: a cycle in which output information is fed back to adjust the process
items.why: Feedback loop = ciclo de feedback: a saída retorna como informação para ajustar o processo.

items.q: "Every manual hand-off between systems is where the delay creeps in." A hand-off is…
options: a point where work or responsibility passes from one party to another
a discount given to a client
items.why: Hand-off = passagem: o ponto em que o trabalho ou a responsabilidade passa de um para o outro.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Two days of extra cycle time may look small, but it opened a ___ our rivals could not close."
items.why: Gap = diferença/lacuna: a distância competitiva que se abriu entre as empresas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de operações e supply chain. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "None of these tweaks will move the needle on our order cycle." To move the needle means to…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível e mensurável.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the cycle-time programme before we start." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the automated hand-offs one region at a time." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on the two-day target, calling it unrealistic." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We agreed the plan last quarter but never followed through on it." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.
